solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: English teaching fundamentals old dons bungle (5)

indicatorNotes.dons: to don is to put on, so RRR puts O on inside it

blocks.note: the three Rs: reading, writing and 'rithmetic

annotation.surface: A complaint that old academics are making a mess of teaching English basics.
annotation.walkthrough: The basics of teaching are the three Rs, RRR; they don O, which lands between the second and third R. 'Dons' looks like university teachers but is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A bungle is a clumsy mistake; error is the plain synonym, noun for noun.

entries.clue: Just beats bridge player lacking hearts with superior advantage (5,3)

indicatorNotes.lacking: to lack something is to be without it, so SOUTH goes without its H
indicatorNotes.with superior: in a down clue the superior piece sits on top, so EDGE comes first

blocks.note: SOUTH, one of the four bridge seats, minus H for hearts

annotation.surface: A bridge report: one player without hearts still narrowly wins thanks to a better position.
annotation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named by compass seat: North, South, East, West. H = hearts, as on a card.
annotation.definitionFit: To edge out a rival is to beat them by a narrow margin.

entries.clue: Coarse humour of novel library finally banned (8)

indicatorNotes.novel: novel means new, so the letters are made new
indicatorNotes.finally: take the last letter of banned

annotation.surface: A book of crude jokes was pulled from the library shelves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' sits beside 'library' pretending to be a book on its shelves; it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Ribaldry is vulgar, bawdy joking: coarse humour.

entries.clue: Fruit I declared second rate covered in mushrooms, causing surprise (7,8)

indicatorNotes.declared: said out loud, so I becomes the word EYE
indicatorNotes.covered in: EYE and B are covered by GROWS, sitting inside it

blocks.note: to mushroom is to grow rapidly; EYEB goes after the G

annotation.surface: Someone boasting that a fruit was second-rate and full of mushrooms, to the dismay of listeners.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mushrooms' is the verb, grows fast, not the fungi. G-ROWS opens to take EYE and B.
annotation.definitionFit: Raising eyebrows is the facial sign of surprise, so an act doing so is causing surprise.

entries.clue: Hare found at sea is unprecedented (7-2)

indicatorNotes.at sea: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A hare discovered swimming in the ocean would be a first.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's absurdity is the point: a hare at sea really would be unheard-of.
annotation.definitionFit: Something unheard-of has never happened before: unprecedented.

entries.clue: Unpleasant using lavatory on vacation (4)

indicatorNotes.on vacation: vacated means emptied, so each word keeps only its outer letters

annotation.surface: A grumble about having to use a grim toilet while on holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' sounds like a holiday; in crosswords vacating a word removes its middle.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the extended sense: an unpleasant scene or mood is called ugly, not just a face.

entries.clue: Illness others take casually (10)

indicatorNotes.casually: done carelessly, so the letters fall in any order

annotation.surface: An illness that other people shrug off.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole wordplay reads as a normal phrase about attitudes, hiding that it is ten letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: heatstroke is one particular illness, brought on by overheating.

entries.clue: American to pile on the pounds and guzzle involuntarily (7,4,4)

blocks.note: to gain weight; a stone is a British unit of body weight, 14 pounds
to swill is to drink greedily

annotation.surface: An American who eats and drinks too much, gaining weight.
annotation.walkthrough: The break falls in an unexpected place: GAIN STONE + SWILL, not STONES + WILL. Britons weigh people in stone, 14 pounds each.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing something against one's will is doing it involuntarily.

entries.clue: Abstracted nest boxes before noon (6)

indicatorNotes.boxes: to box something is to enclose it, so DREY holds AM

blocks.note: a drey is a squirrel's nest

annotation.surface: Nest boxes put up in the morning, with a hint that someone is distracted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nest boxes' looks like a bird-box noun phrase, but 'boxes' is the verb. A drey is a squirrel's nest.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone abstracted is lost in thought: dreamy.

entries.clue: Thing from buffet is horrendous (6)

indicatorNotes.from: the answer is taken out of the words that follow

annotation.surface: Someone declaring the thing on the buffet table awful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thing' means an obsession, as in having a thing about shoes.
annotation.definitionFit: A fetish is an obsessive fixation, informally a thing.

entries.clue: Lady Georgia everyone recalled eating cheese (9)

indicatorNotes.recalled: called back, so ALL runs backwards
indicatorNotes.eating: GA and LLA take BRIE inside them

blocks.note: GA is the US postal abbreviation for Georgia

annotation.surface: A woman from Georgia whom everyone remembers eating cheese.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lady Georgia' reads as a titled woman, but 'Lady' alone is the definition, a woman's name.
annotation.definitionFit: Gabriella is a woman's name; a lady is a woman.

entries.clue: Vigilant group from regiment relaxed having retreated (5)

indicatorNotes.group from: a group of letters taken from the words that follow
indicatorNotes.having retreated: going backwards, so the letters read right to left

annotation.surface: A watchful unit of soldiers pulled back and eased off.
annotation.walkthrough: The military surface makes 'retreated' look like troops withdrawing; it tells you to read TRELA backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a vigilant guard is an alert one, keeping watch for danger.

entries.clue: Drip of fluid going over plant (6)

indicatorNotes.going over: going over means turning over, and the turned drip goes back into the fluid

blocks.note: SALIVA, a bodily fluid, with its IV lifted out
an IV is an intravenous drip

annotation.surface: A drip of liquid running over a plant, as in watering.
annotation.walkthrough: The drip is already inside the fluid: only it turns over, in place. Salvia is the sage family of garden plants.
annotation.definitionFit: Salvia is a flowering plant, the sage genus.

entries.clue: Great volumes of letters backing Albert Camus, a French author (8)

indicatorNotes.letters backing: the letters at the back of each name, their last letters

blocks.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, British novelists

annotation.surface: A literary note about the big collection of letters supporting the French writer Camus.
annotation.walkthrough: Camus looks like the author, but 'author' is AMIS, the British novelists Kingsley and Martin. 'Great volumes' sounds like books; it means huge quantities.
annotation.definitionFit: Tsunamis are huge surges of water, so great volumes of it.

entries.clue: Curious wearing on parts proven reliable (10)

indicatorNotes.parts: RE parts TESTED, splitting it into TE and STED

blocks.note: in a coat = wearing a coat

annotation.surface: Something odd about wearing parts that have been proven sound.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parts' looks like a noun, components; it is the verb, splitting the longer word to let the short one in.
annotation.definitionFit: Curious means wanting to know, interested.

entries.clue: Obstinate duo — nurses, they regularly skipped nursing classes (12)

indicatorNotes.nursing: UNRE…TE holds GENERA as a nurse holds a baby

blocks.note: dUo NuRsEs ThEy: the even letters

annotation.surface: A stubborn pair of nurses who skipped their training classes.
annotation.walkthrough: The alternate letters run straight across the dash and comma: d-U-o-N-u-R-s-E-s-T-h-E-y. Two different 'nurs' words sit side by side, one fodder and one indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Unregenerate means unreformed and stubbornly unrepentant: obstinate.

entries.clue: Atheistic rogue ignoring lead authority in moral standards (8)

indicatorNotes.rogue: a rogue element behaves unpredictably and out of line, so the letters do not keep their places
indicatorNotes.ignoring lead: drop the first letter, the A of atheistic

annotation.surface: A godless scoundrel who rejects the lead of a moral authority.
annotation.walkthrough: Nice irony: removing the A turns atheistic into theistic before the shuffle.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: an ethicist is a specialist whose field is moral standards, so an expert voice on them.

entries.clue: Lebanon-based compere is comedian (8)

blocks.note: based in Tyre, a city in Lebanon

annotation.surface: A master of ceremonies working in Lebanon turns out to be a comic.
annotation.walkthrough: Michael McIntyre is a popular British stand-up comedian. The compere comes first, then where he is based: MC IN TYRE.
annotation.definitionFit: Michael McIntyre is a well-known British comedian.

entries.clue: Ink they ordered with price moving excessively (12)

indicatorNotes.ordered: ordered in the sense of arranged in a sequence, so the letters are put into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone buying ink with the cost going up far too fast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' seems to mean purchased, beside 'ink' and 'price'; it means rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Hyperkinetic means abnormally or excessively active in movement.

entries.clue: Peak in Snowdonia cold Welshman climbed (6)

indicatorNotes.Peak in: in a down clue the peak of a word is its top, first letter

blocks.note: first letter of Snowdonia, its top in a down clue
C = cold, as on a tap
Aled is a common Welsh man's name, as in singer Aled Jones

annotation.surface: A Welshman climbing a peak in Snowdonia, the Welsh mountain area, in the cold.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is a mountaineering scene, so 'Peak' reads as a summit; it means the top letter.
annotation.definitionFit: To scale a mountain is to climb it.

entries.clue: Earth ridge shelters ancient city (6)

blocks.note: the brow of a hill is a ridge
Ur of the Chaldees, in Mesopotamia

annotation.surface: A ridge of ground that has protected an old city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Earth' is a fox's den, not soil.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword favourite: a fox's den is called its earth, and that hole in the ground is a burrow.

entries.clue: Last of public spirit drained and crushed (8)

indicatorNotes.Last of: the last of anything is its final part, so of a word its final letter

annotation.surface: The last shred of public morale was exhausted and flattened.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Public spirit' reads as civic morale; split it, and 'spirit' is the drink RUM.
annotation.definitionFit: Crumbled means broken into pieces, crushed.

entries.clue: Set cycling is safely turning around corners (6)

indicatorNotes.turning: something turning round faces the other way, so the letters read right to left
indicatorNotes.around corners: the letters run around the corners between words, across three of them

annotation.surface: Advice on cycling safely: take the corners slowly as you turn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' looks like an instruction to rotate letters, but it is only where the hidden letters start.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to set someone homework is to assign it to them.

entries.clue: Olympian challenges eliminating beginner (4)

indicatorNotes.eliminating beginner: the beginner of a word is its first letter, and eliminating it knocks that letter out

blocks.note: DARES (challenges) without its first letter D

annotation.surface: An Olympic athlete knocking out a novice in a contest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' suggests an athlete; here it is a god of Mount Olympus, Ares, the Greek god of war.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the Olympians were the gods of Mount Olympus, and Ares, god of war, was one.

entries.clue: Slowly left ship (5)

annotation.surface: A ship pulling away from the dock at a leisurely pace.
annotation.walkthrough: Largo is the musical direction for a slow, broad tempo.
annotation.definitionFit: Largo in music means to be played slowly.

entries.clue: Laziness of Conservative penning papers in bed (9)

indicatorNotes.in: in places one thing inside another, so ID sits inside PIT

blocks.note: a Tory is a British Conservative

annotation.surface: A lazy Tory politician doing his paperwork from bed.
annotation.walkthrough: Two layers: ID goes into PIT, then PIDIT goes into TORY. 'Pit' is British slang for bed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: torpidity is sluggish inactivity, the state of a lazy person.

entries.clue: Blue team’s flaws (9)

annotation.surface: The faults of a sports team in blue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blue team' suggests a kit colour; blue is a mood, DOWN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the downsides of a plan are its drawbacks or weak points.

entries.clue: Flexible movement of snake sloughing skin (5)

indicatorNotes.sloughing skin: snakes slough their skin; here the word sheds its outer letters

blocks.note: a snake's movement is to SLITHER; drop its outer letters S and R

annotation.surface: A snake moving supply as it sheds its old skin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flexible movement' looks like one phrase; the definition is just 'Flexible'. The snake image fits the indicator perfectly.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a lithe body bends easily and gracefully, like a snake's.
